input: Find a local grief support group to attend

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Grief support groups vary widely — some focus on specific types of loss (spouse, child, parent, pet, suicide loss). Knowing the type of loss shapes which groups are actually relevant.
Location determines which groups are geographically accessible. Without knowing their city or region, no real search can begin.
Groups meet at different times — weekday evenings, weekends, daytime. The user's availability determines which sessions they can actually attend.
Some groups are free (nonprofit, religious, hospital-based) while others charge fees. Budget affects which options are viable.
Some people want a faith-based group; others prefer secular. Some want a structured program (like GriefShare); others want open peer discussion. This shapes the right fit.
Some groups are age-specific (teens, adults, seniors) or loss-specific (widows/widowers, bereaved parents). Knowing who the group is for ensures a comfortable, relevant match.
The user's definition of 'done' matters — is success finding one group to try, or vetting several options and committing to one after a first visit?

gold.taskTitle: Find and join a local grief support group
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to locate a grief support group in their area and start attending it.

questions.title: What type of loss are you seeking support for?
questions.description: Identify the specific type of loss (e.g., spouse, parent, child, sibling, friend, pet, loss to suicide) so the search can be narrowed to groups designed for that experience.

questions.title: What city or area should the group be near?
questions.description: Establish the user's location or preferred travel radius so that only geographically accessible groups are surfaced.

questions.title: Which days or times are you free to attend?
questions.description: Determine the user's weekly availability — weekday evenings, weekends, daytime — so only groups with compatible meeting schedules are considered.

questions.title: Is cost a factor, or do you need a free group?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user needs a no-cost option or is open to groups with fees, so paid programs are included or excluded accordingly.

questions.title: Do you prefer a faith-based or secular environment?
questions.description: Understand whether the user wants a religiously affiliated group, a strictly secular one, or has no preference, to match their comfort level.

questions.title: Is the group for you personally or someone else?
questions.description: Find out if the user is seeking a group for themselves or helping someone else (e.g., a child, elderly parent, or friend), which affects age range and group format requirements.

questions.title: What would make this task feel complete to you?
questions.description: Establish what 'done' looks like — whether the goal is simply to identify a list of options, register for a group, or actually attend a first session.
